Subject: FastShip — tokenflow calibration & streaming requirements (post-demo follow-up)

Thanks again for the demo time today, Tom and Emily — great conversation. Quick recap and a few clarifying asks so we can size a trial cluster and prep the dedicated throughput estimate: 

1) Observed / expected traffic
- You mentioned a steady-state of ~60 QPS to the summarization endpoint and short peak spikes up to ~750 QPS for ~10 minutes during end-of-day batch pushes. Please confirm whether that 750 QPS is at the API request level (i.e., http requests/sec) or at the token emission rate.

2) Payloads and token sizes
- You indicated average request payloads around 1,200 tokens and some interactive flows that stream partial results. Can you share representative payloads (we asked for examples on the call).

3) Latency SLOs
- You said product wants p95 <= 250ms for interactive flows and p95 <= 500ms is acceptable for background batch jobs. Confirm for us which endpoints get which SLOs.

4) Streaming & concurrency
- Clarify the proportion of requests that will use streaming (progressive summarization) vs non-streaming generation. Also we need an estimate of concurrent streaming connections (you mentioned ~200 simultaneous streams during peak).

5) Isolation & retention
- Will you require tenant isolation (per-customer runtime) for the pilot? Any retention/compliance constraints we should account for?

Next steps we propose:
- You share two sample payloads and a representative peak 10-minute traffic CSV (qps over time).
- We run a targeted sizing exercise and deliver a short RID (recommended instance/dedicated pool) + cost estimate within 3 business days.
- Schedule a tech-deep-dive (30–45m) to validate streaming performance assumptions.

I attached the short call notes and a sample payload template to make it easy to drop-in examples. Thanks — I’ll ping to align calendars for the tech deep-dive once we have your payloads.

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple of clarifications and I attached a short CSV with the 10-minute peak sample and some logs.

1) The 750 number is QPS at the HTTP request level (not tokens/sec). Those spikes are concentrated around 13:00 PST as nightly aggregation jobs finish and push user-facing notifications (10–12 minutes typically).

2) Average request size: 1,200 tokens (compressed) — we occasionally have heavier requests up to ~4,000 tokens for long document summarizations. Median per-request response length is ~600 tokens.

3) Streaming: ~30% of interactive flows use streaming; these are the ones that must hit p95 <= 250ms for the first response byte (we will accept slightly higher end-to-end generation latency for long responses). Estimated concurrent streaming sessions: peak ~180–220 (we quoted ~200 earlier).

4) Concurrency: Beyond streams, we have background batch jobs that fan out many short requests; concurrency at peak could be ~1,000 short-lived connections during the 10-minute window.

5) Isolation: Pilot does not require strict per-tenant runtime isolation — logical separation is fine. Retention: logs retained 90 days; payloads are non-sensitive.

Attached: fastship-peak-window-logs.csv (10-minute QPS sample).

Tom

Thanks Tom — good detail. Quick math and a couple of follow-ups from our side before sizing: 

- If peak is 750 QPS (http requests/sec) and median response is ~600 tokens, that’s ~450k tokens/sec sustained through the peak window (750 * 600). If we plan for a safety factor of 1.5 for bursts and model overhead, we should design for ~675k tokens/sec during the peak window.

- For streaming connections: 200 concurrent streams with an average emission rate of ~40 tokens/sec would add ~8k tokens/sec; streaming memory (KV cache) will increase per-session footprint.

Questions: 
1) Which model tier are you aiming to use in pilot? (higher-capacity LLMs change GPU/inference throughput assumptions significantly).
2) Are you willing to enable prefix caching for repeated prompts? That reduces token compute for many of your notifications.
3) Do you expect long-tail requests (4k tokens) to be a meaningful percent of traffic, or are those rare outliers?

We’ll draft a recommended cluster config (GPU types, instance counts, batching targets) once we have answers — target to ship tomorrow afternoon.

—
